mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.25% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS has increased over the past three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals a contraction in supply, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic output and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in the last month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 jobs within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% over the past two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending improve.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% QoQ and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 grew by more than 2% QoQ and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% within the last month.
